title: Acceleration during pulling
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the net force during the first 2 seconds (applied force minus kinetic friction) and divides by mass to find acceleration (6 m/s²).

title: Velocity at t=2s
description: Important: Uses kinematic equation (v = a₁t) with the correct acceleration and time to find the velocity at the moment the force is removed (12 m/s).

title: Kinetic energy calculation
description: Essential: Correctly applies the kinetic energy formula (½mv²) using the mass and the velocity found at t=2s to obtain the final value (144 J).

title: Post-force acceleration
description: Important: Recognizes that after the force is removed, the only horizontal force is kinetic friction, and correctly calculates the deceleration (a₂ = μ g = 2 m/s²).

title: Sliding distance calculation
description: Essential: Correctly uses a kinematic equation (v_f² = v_i² + 2a x) with final velocity zero, initial velocity from part (2), and deceleration from part (4) to find the sliding distance (36 m).

title: Friction force error
description: Pitfall: Uses the wrong coefficient (static instead of kinetic) or incorrectly calculates the friction force (e.g., forgetting g or mass).

title: Sign/vector confusion
description: Pitfall: Mishandles signs in the kinematic equations for the deceleration phase, leading to a negative or incorrect distance.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Demonstrates consistent use of SI units (kg, m, s, N, J) throughout the solution without conversion errors.
